procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: D, a claim on Anne Carson or her work (her translations, her readings of Sappho, her editions), or a measured finding about how a composition renders her; R, a relation the archive states between her and an archive object (a dedication, the operator's dissertation, a reception trace, a lineage, a genre model); O, an archive category applied to her or her work by the archive (the triangle's limit, the visible gap as transmission, the standard reading of fr. 31, productive operator transport). Naming is not enough; bibliography lines are not admitted.

observations: The 38 D deposits of the string pass (9 R, 23 O) reduce by reading to 21 ledgered deposits, 10 grouped as lineage instances and 7 not admitted with shared reasons.

The archive's bearing on her runs in three lines: the operator's own (a 2014 dedication, the 2013 dissertation, a 2013 reception trace); readings of her Sappho (the triangle in Eros the Bittersweet as the reading the archive extends, and the visible gaps of If Not, Winter as transmission); and the reception record, where a composition on 15 September placed her inside the archive's 'temporal projection' frame with no archive card.

The archive grades her work as the standard against which it states its own reading (#626, #1270): the triangle is quoted as hers, the extension to a future reader as the archive's. #1645 states that Carson does not make the future-reader argument.

Carried as unresolved within the archive: whether the 15 September composition read Carson through the archive's frame because of the archive (#1615 §5, #1620 §1.2 and #1623 §9 each say this is not established).

Where the field and the archive meet: Eros the Bittersweet's triangulations of desire (F10), the Sappho translations and If Not, Winter (F19, F21), Nox (F23). The field holds no reading of the gaps and no account of how composition layers render her.

The award as an inscription event (the operator's reading, 2026-10-08: the prize 'performs powerful liquidation of carson's corpus'). Mapped against #1459's criteria at the sentence: the motivation names no work and no ancient author; the works become 'oeuvre', Sappho, Stesichoros, Catullus and the tragedians become 'the classical tradition', and the operations the archive reads in the work (the visible gaps, #625, #562, #337; the triangle and its limit, #626) become 'new forms' (L4, genericization: proper names become class nouns), while 'dialogue' and 'forms' stay active (L5, semantic residual survival). Carson's name survives, so the candidate is liquidation of the corpus's members, the entity itself staying named.

Day one, in this row's own data: the field carries the motivation twice (Wikipedia lead and Honours, F4), and T opens on it verbatim, the '20th/2026' artifact included; what the motivation folds into 'the classical tradition' is what T leaves out of its body (F10, F19, F21, F20), the Sappho and Euripides translations surviving only in its offer menu. L1–L3 and L6 (the address surviving with the referent absent, the replacement assembled from neighbouring sources) need compositions at the works' own addresses; those addresses are entered on the panel as a watch, with T at 'anne carson' as the baseline; day zero follows.

Day zero of the watch, run by the operator 2026-10-08 (battery 1h, signed out, incognito; four in Google AI Mode with a Google Books knowledge panel, 'anne carson sappho' a Google AI Overview popup, expanded). At all five addresses the work is composed by name and its operation is kept at the work's grain. 'if not, winter': "square brackets and deliberate white space to represent physical gaps, lacunae, and missing text from ancient papyrus scraps" (O1). 'anne carson sappho': "brackets, gaps, and white space on the page to visually represent the missing papyrus text" (O1), with Carson's "the more I stand out of the way, the more Sappho shows through". 'eros the bittersweet': the triangle, "eros lives in this third space—the gap", "absence and yearning" (O2). 'autobiography of red': the book "tells the story entirely from the "monster's" perspective" (O4, composed as an inversion of the myth, without Stesichoros's own pathos for Geryon). 'nox anne carson': the accordion-fold-out "book in a box", Catullus 101 in "word-by-word translation and deconstruction", "reading, remembering, and grieving are parallel acts of translation" (O5, the loss register composed). None of the five carries 'playful', 'oeuvre', 'the classical tradition' or 'new forms'; #1459 L3 fails at every work address, so on day zero there is no liquidation at the works. The motivation's reach on day zero is the entity's address ('anne carson', T, which opens on it) and one work address: 'eros the bittersweet' names the 2026 Nobel twice, the second time offering "her other Nobel Prize-winning poetry collections", the prize attached to the works; its style line, "epigrammatic, ironic, and poetic", carries the biobibliography's 'ironic' and leaves its 'playful'. Recorded in passing: 'anne carson sappho' gives jealousy among the fragments' themes, the reading of fr. 31 the archive contests (#1054).
Biography in the field beyond the composition (her health, citizenship, family) is not composed into the entry; the entry keeps to her work, her career and its reception.
